audit.whatIsWrong: Page called this TRICKY at 7.5/10 while the mirror had already settled it as EVEN at 5/10, and while the chart handed Graves four of seven stages with Poppy still winning 52.62%.
audit.why: The packet's own defect note flagged the contradiction. The mirror's resolution is that Graves owns the middle of the lane on range and Quickdraw uptime, but Poppy's win rate comes from the fight leaving open ground — chokes, walls and teamfights. That is an even matchup, not a tricky one.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, tone recoloured, diffRating 6/10, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14] updated to match. Graves's carry threat stays 8/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Graves / Skill / Poppy / Poppy / Graves / Poppy / Poppy in both layers — nothing like the mirror's already-applied order or the packet's.
audit.why: Mirror point 2 set both layers to Skill / Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill at 5,5,7,7,7,7,5. Those ratings are from Graves's page, so ours invert to 5,5,3,3,3,3,5. The whys for rows 2-6 described the opposite lane and had to be rewritten to match, or the page would render a chart that argues with its own explanations.
audit.corrected: All seven rows proposed as one atomic group across both layers, with ratings and every affected why and phase text rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated Quickdraw as a normal cooldown to wait out — 'Engage when it's down', 'Poppy wins the Quickdraw cooldown windows'. Quickdraw's cooldown is reduced every time Graves lands a basic attack, so against a Graves who is hitting you it is almost never down.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill and refreshes the resistance boost.' That inverts the whole plan — you bait Quickdraw and eat it with Steadfast Presence, you do not wait for it. W is 20s at rank 1 against his 16s, so you cannot parry every dash either.
audit.corrected: Stated in tldr, phases[1..3].why, whys[2], dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and breakdown.cooldowns, with both cooldowns given.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere, and Smoke Screen was described as a blind in three fields.
audit.why: Smoke Screen 'reduces sight range' with an impact slow and magic damage — it is a vision cut, not a blind. The mirror agent reframed it the same way from the other side. End of the Line is 925 range and detonates on terrain contact, which is why standing with a wall at your back is punishing.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt with Quickdraw 16/15/14/13/12s, Smoke Screen 26/24/22/20/18s and Collateral Damage 100/80/60s; dontsFull[2].d now states the terrain detonation.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid opened 'Levels 4-6 are your strongest stretch', directly contradicting the corrected chart.
audit.why: Those are the levels Graves owns on range and dash uptime. Poppy's win condition is terrain and teamfights, which is what the late paragraph already says correctly.
audit.corrected: mid rewritten to concede the stretch while keeping the real W-eats-Quickdraw interaction.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Quickdraw's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: End of the Line reaches 925 and detonates on terrain — he controls the range here, so farm safe and wait for a dash mistake.

edits.after: It evens out — drag him into chokes where E and R land instead of duelling in open ground. Graves carry threat 8/10.

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by whether you fight him in chokes and on walls or in open ground.

edits.after: Your kit is online, but Quickdraw (16s) refreshes off his autos, so he holds the dash and stays outside your 475 E range.

edits.before: Your Q percent-HP and W dash-grounding out-trade him while his points-in-W damage scaling can't keep up with your disruption.
edits.after: He pokes from 925 with End of the Line and resets Quickdraw by hitting you, so he owns the range and you just eat the chip.

edits.before: Keeper's Verdict charge-stops his E reposition and can knock him out of his own Smoke Screen for the kill.
edits.after: Collateral Damage (100s) out-bursts you at 6, and Smoke Screen's sight cut makes your wall angle a guess.

edits.before: Cheap bruiser components plus W's free armor let you walk his shotgun autos and E-stun him on every cooldown.
edits.after: His first item turns the shotgun into real burst while your components only buy resists — this window is his.

edits.before: He out-scales with shotgun burst and stacked armor — fight him on walls and in chokes, not in an open kite, and peel instead of duel.
edits.after: It levels out late — he out-duels you in open ground, but your W, E wall-stun and max-HP Q win any fight you drag into a choke.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your strongest stretch. Your W (Steadfast Presence) is the answer to his whole escape plan: pop it as he tries to E away or through you and you ground the dash, stop it dead, and slow him into your E-wall-stun. Q keeps chunking him through the armor he's stacking. At 6, Keeper's Verdict charge-stops his reposition or knocks him out of his own Smoke Screen — use it to seal an all-in, not to poke.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are his stretch, not yours — End of the Line pokes from 925 and Quickdraw refreshes off every auto he lands, so it is rarely down to punish. Your W (Steadfast Presence) is still the answer to his escape: pop it as he E's away or through you and the dash dies, leaving him slowed and grounded for the wall-stun. At 6 respect Collateral Damage, and save Keeper's Verdict to break his reposition rather than to poke.

notes: This chart flip is the one place I went against the surface reading of the data, so it is worth the user's eye: the packet itself carries the defect 'level chart contradicts data: Poppy wins 52.62% but the chart gives Graves 4/7 stages vs 0'. The mirror agent resolved it by keeping the packet chart and calling the matchup EVEN, on the reasoning that Graves owns the lane phase while Poppy's win rate comes from everything after it. I followed the mirror rather than fight it, and rewrote five whys and six phase texts so the explanations no longer argue with the chart. If the user disagrees with that resolution, both pages need changing together, not just this one.
